set.pl: 2 mi E of Bronson (Battle Creek Enquirer 17 Jul 1939; the AP's "4 mi W" was wrong); farm not yet placed on a plat
pinev: Placeholder: GNIS Bronson moved 2 mi east on the same line, per the local Battle Creek Enquirer (17 Jul 1939 p1); about 1.2 km until the plat check.
set.st: July 1939: the three young Belote boys dug up a drain tile holding $1,880 in $5/$10/$20 gold (1882-1902) on the farm 2 mi E of Bronson; days later Frank Belote kicked up an iron pipe with $1,120 in gold 12 ft away. A second tile, plugged with concrete at both ends, which the boys had used as a toy smokestack, was never found again. Owner Kregger ordered no more digging and evicted the Belotes. The original owner, who died in 1904, was said to have buried several lots of gold; a buried safe was dug up on the farm 25+ years before 1939, and the owner had plowed up a pipe of gold the year before the tile find. Pin is a placeholder about 2 mi E of Bronson until the plat check, not the spot itself.
set.t: Strong site: two caches 12 ft apart in the house yard; a third plugged tile is unaccounted for. Find the Kregger farm on a 1930s Branch County plat (Bronson Twp, about 2 mi E of town), check the house yard on the 1938-40 aerial. Access: private farm: permission.
src: Coldwater-area paper on the eviction (TN thread)
